reader.requirement: An elementary item with no USAGE clause on itself or on any group containing it takes usage DISPLAY, while an item under a group that writes a usage takes that usage (GR1), at every nesting depth; the witness covers only the no-clause-anywhere case against an explicit DISPLAY.

reader.notes: One derivation gives the effective usage: own clause, else nearest enclosing group's, else DISPLAY. FUNCTION LENGTH, legal at 85 only inside an arithmetic expression (COMPUTE), measured the widths. COMP-5 is accepted at --std 85 as an extension, which this rule does not reach.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-105/src/g6a.cob at --std 85 (g6a-001): 01 RG REDEFINES a USAGE COMP group gives LRG=0004 and LR1=0002, so the redefining X(2) leaves are DISPLAY and do not inherit COMP. 66 RENAMES over PACKED leaves gives LPR=0004. An explicit USAGE DISPLAY group with a nested leaf gives LDG=0008. A BINARY subgroup beside a no-usage sibling gives LCGB=0006 and CGB2=-0012. Records of an EXTERNAL FD share one area: EB=WX EC=YZ. In g6c and g6d, PIC 1(8), whose usage is implicitly BIT from 2002, is refused at 85 with COBOL0900, and so is GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.5.14.4 GR6  (5.14.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR6.
